podcast.title: A&R Superstar
podcast.body: Nate Albert is recognized as a "superstar of A&R" for his pivotal role in discovering The Weeknd. He successfully secured The Weeknd's signing to Capital Music Group despite more than two dozen competing offers from other labels. "Take Nate Albert. He was the one who found the weekend and then fended off more than two dozen competing offers to sign up to Capital Music Group."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Former Band Member
podcast.body: He is a former member of the band The Mighty Mighty Bosstones, where he played guitar. This background gives him a unique perspective on the music industry from both an artistic and executive standpoint. "Nate is a former member of the mighty, mighty boss tones. He played guitar on songs like this."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Nate Albert's Membership
xref.body: Nate Albert, who later became a prominent A&R executive, played guitar for The Mighty Mighty Bosstones. His involvement in the band is mentioned in the context of his A&R career. "Nate is a former member of the mighty, mighty boss tones. He played guitar on songs like this."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: YouTube Discovery and Signing (Capital Music Group)
xref.body: The Weeknd was first discovered on YouTube. Nate Albert, an A&R executive, was instrumental in finding him and subsequently fending off more than two dozen competing offers to sign him to Capital Music Group. "The Weekend... they were all first found on YouTube."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
